high CRP levels measured upon admission are associated with the severity and extension of coronary lesions in acute coronary syndome.
CRP and fibrionogen levels measured upon hospital admission in patients presenting with acute coronary syndomes are associated with the severity and the extent of the coronary lesions.
high plasma CRP and fibrineogen levels are associated with the presence of significant and proximal coronary artery lesions.

the predictive value of the markers for inflammation in patients presenting with acute coronary syndomes.
the predictive value of CRP and fibrigen levels in the presence of significant lesions in acute coronary syndomes.
the predictive value of CRP level in the presence of significant lesions and the severity of acute coronary syndroms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRP and fibriong levels upon admission are predictive factors of the severity and extension of the coronary lesions in patients presenting with an ACS.
the CRP level measured upon admission in acute coronary syndrome patients is an important independent predictor of the presence of coronary lesions and of the severity of the lesions.
CRP and fibrinegon are associated with the severity of coronary disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRP and fibrigen levels measured in the acute phase of coronary syndrome are independent predictors of the extent, severity and proximal localization of coronary lesions.
the CRP and fibrigen plasma levels measured upon admission are predictive factors of the severity of the lesions of coronary arteries in patients presenting with an ACS.
the CRP level is a good marker for the severity and the extent of coronary lesions in acute coronary syndomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRP and fibrineogen are independent markers of coronary lesions severity.

the measurement of the markers of acute phase reaction upon admission in patients presenting with acute coronary syndome is a simple, non invasive, cheap and reliable method for the evaluation of the severity of coronary lesion and the prognosis of these patients.

CRP and fibrinegon levels measured upon admission could be used as a marker of the extent and severity of coronary lesions and could be used to guide the decision to perform coronary angiography in patients with acute chest pain.
